reading: Engagement is shaped before, during and after install: access to a device and data (claim c4), the effort and fit of the app, and whether anyone at clinic looks at the entries (claim c3). Measures of engagement are inconsistent (claim c2) and engagement decays within months (claim c1), so any claim that engagement improves outcomes rests on thin ground. The clinic's choice between coaching and building an app depends on which of these links the literature describes.

nodes.label: Access to a smartphone and data
nodes.detail: Lower in older and low-income patients (claim c4).

nodes.label: Sustained engagement
nodes.detail: Falls from 61 to 14 percent over a year (claim c1).

nodes.label: Adherence and seizure recording
nodes.detail: Linked to engagement in small studies only.

summary: Map of access, features and clinician response feeding engagement, with inconsistent definitions blocking the link to outcomes.
